benchmark_articles.title: NovaTech Launches Orion Laptop With 18-Hour Battery
benchmark_articles.article: NovaTech has launched the Orion, a new laptop designed for students and professionals. The laptop uses the company's NovaCore X2 processor, includes 16GB of RAM and 512GB of storage, and has a 14-inch display. NovaTech says the Orion can provide up to 18 hours of battery life under typical usage. The laptop starts at $899 and will be available from October 15 in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. The company said the device is aimed at users who need long battery life for work and study. NovaTech has not yet announced when the laptop will become available in other regions.

benchmark_articles.title: City Council Approves Public Transport Expansion Plan
benchmark_articles.article: The Riverton City Council has approved a three-year public transport expansion plan following a public meeting on Tuesday. The plan includes 25 new electric buses, six additional routes, and 40 new bus stops across the city. According to the council, the project will cost approximately $18 million and will be funded through a combination of city funds and a regional transportation grant. Construction and route preparation are expected to begin in January. Council officials said the expansion is intended to improve access to public transportation in neighborhoods that currently have limited service. The council has not provided a final completion date for all six routes.

benchmark_articles.title: Harbor City Wins National Basketball Final
benchmark_articles.article: Harbor City defeated Metro United 92-87 in the National Basketball Final on Saturday to win its first championship in eight years. Harbor City led 48-43 at halftime and maintained its advantage through the final quarter. Guard Daniel Reed scored 27 points for Harbor City, while forward Marcus Lee added 19 points and 11 rebounds. Metro United was led by James Carter, who scored 24 points. The final was played in front of 14,200 spectators at Central Arena. Harbor City coach Elena Torres said the team's defensive performance in the second half was important to the victory.

benchmark_articles.title: GreenMart Opens New Distribution Center
benchmark_articles.article: Retail company GreenMart has opened a new distribution center in Eastport as part of its plan to expand its regional delivery network. The facility covers 180,000 square feet and employs approximately 320 workers. GreenMart invested $42 million in the center, which will supply stores across three states. The company said the facility uses automated sorting systems to improve package processing speed. Operations began on Monday, and GreenMart expects the center to handle up to 50,000 packages per day once it reaches full capacity. The company said it is considering additional distribution centers but has not announced specific locations.

benchmark_articles.title: Researchers Develop Low-Cost Water Testing Device
benchmark_articles.article: Researchers at the North Valley Institute have developed a portable device that can test drinking water for three common contaminants. The device uses a paper-based sensor and produces results in approximately 15 minutes. In an initial laboratory study involving 120 water samples, the researchers reported that the device correctly identified the target contaminants in 112 samples. The team said the device is designed to reduce the cost of basic water testing in areas where laboratory facilities are limited. The researchers are planning a larger field study next year. The device is still experimental and is not currently approved for official drinking water certification.

benchmark_articles.title: Coastal Town Begins Mangrove Restoration Project
benchmark_articles.article: The coastal town of Bayhaven has begun a mangrove restoration project covering 60 hectares of damaged shoreline. The project is being led by the Bayhaven Environmental Department with support from local fishing groups and two universities. Officials said the first phase will involve planting approximately 45,000 mangrove seedlings over six months. The project is intended to restore coastal habitat and reduce shoreline erosion. Monitoring teams will record seedling survival rates every three months. The environmental department said the project will be evaluated after two years before decisions are made about expanding it to other parts of the coastline.
